answer: In PoA, each identity is backed by bonded escrow. Evidence of equivocation among k coordinated identities triggers pairwise penalties proportional to k(k−1)/2, or O(k²). Upon detection, asymmetric depreciation compounds across implicated escrows, applying an exponential multiplier to swarm-wide capital loss; splitting stake among names does not evade aggregate liability. A beacon may reveal shared timing across a grove of keys, while an inlet preserves signed conflicting votes as proof.
